paragraphs: Friend, here's the big idea. The LORD's blessings are meant to point you back to the LORD. Moses says the wilderness was there to humble Israel and test them, and the manna taught them that "man does not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD" (Deuteronomy 8:3). Even the hard stretch had a purpose, because the LORD humbled and tested them "so that in the end He might cause you to prosper" (Deuteronomy 8:16).

Now here's the sneaky part, and I want you to hear it. Moses isn't most worried about the hungry days. He's worried about the full ones, when you eat and are satisfied, build fine houses and watch everything multiply (Deuteronomy 8:12-13). That's when a heart can say, "The power and strength of my hands have made this wealth for me" (Deuteronomy 8:17). Friend, I've said "I made that batch" while the oven did the heavy lifting.

So Moses gives the cure, and it's simple: remember. He says to "remember that it is the LORD your God who gives you the power to gain wealth" (Deuteronomy 8:18). When you eat and are satisfied, bless Him (Deuteronomy 8:10). Whatever is on your plate or in your bank account today, say thank you to the One who gave it, and keep His Word as your daily bread.
